claims.conditions: A runnable target (browser application, API, CLI, job, worker or webhook) in a Claude Code session with the gstack distribution installed under ~/.claude/skills/gstack, where the agent may write under the report directory and the gstack state root. The target and mode are known or inferable; the user may be away afterwards. Invocation must already be permitted by the user, the harness and applicable policy; this claim describes suitability under the stated conditions and grants no permission to invoke.
claims.rationale: The source states 'NEVER fix anything or change product tests' and 'Write only reports, evidence and owned temporary fixtures' (lines 130-131) and, in its own rules, 'Do not edit product code, tests, dependencies, config or tracked state through any tool, including shell writes, renames, deletions and edit-then-restore. Never commit, stash or bootstrap' (lines 333-336). It forbids chaining: 'Never invoke /qa or another skill from this report-only run' (line 339), and it writes probe charters into the report before probing (line 244). In the inspected file the questions it directs are for an unknown target or a mode conflict (lines 155-164). Tracked product files are to be left as found, which bounds what a model-led run can change there. Qualifications: surface selection, probing and reporting are defined in section files that were not read (lines 144-145), so further questions or writes may be directed there; the shared startup section still writes question logs and analytics under the state root, so 'report-only' describes the product repository and not the machine; and probing an API, job or webhook is not read-only for the system under test, which the no-write rules do not cover. Falsified if tracked files or git state differ after a run, the skill's own reports, evidence and temporary fixtures aside; qualified if probes are shown to mutate the target system's data.
